action: Vanderbilt students and staff: follow university instructions before reconnecting devices, change passwords when asked, and watch for phishing that references the incident.
date_note: Incident began Nov 9; this entry reflects recovery reporting on Nov 13
exec: A major research university is operating with restricted systems; the data-theft claim is unverified but would be large if true.
impact: Most university systems and applications were restricted; classes and student services continued.
plain: Vanderbilt University shut down many computer systems after a ransomware attack. A criminal group claims it stole a million people's details; the university has not confirmed that.
summary: Vanderbilt told students and staff on November 9 to shut down university devices and leave campus Wi-Fi during an active cybersecurity incident, and access to most systems stayed restricted. The BYOD ransomware group claims it locked databases and took more than 1 million Social Security numbers and contact details. The university has not confirmed the group's involvement or any data theft. Vanderbilt Health's own systems were unaffected.
title: Vanderbilt University restricts systems after ransomware attack; BYOD group claims 1 million records

validation.note: One outlet read in full, citing Axios and BleepingComputer; the theft claim is unconfirmed by the university.
